previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of chronic graft-versus-host disease, hypogammaglobulinemia, and prior stem cell transplant was admitted with diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and fever. She was found to have acute sigmoid diverticulitis on CT imaging and was diagnosed with Salmonella gastroenteritis after stool culture confirmed the pathogen. Due to her immunocompromised state, she was treated with intravenous then oral ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. She developed transient hypotension requiring pressors, and evaluation revealed adrenal insufficiency likely due to chronic prednisone use; her steroid dose was adjusted accordingly. Her mental status improved from encephalopathy, and she regained strength over the hospitalization. She was discharged home on a full course of antibiotics, with plans to follow up for ocular GVHD, adrenal function, and ongoing management of chronic conditions including anticoagulation and IVIG infusions.
